fatal_errors: The proposed chemically homogeneous, random HEA microstructure contradicts the observed solidification-segregated, two-BCC-phase structure with W-Ta-rich dendrites and Zr-Ti-rich interdendritic regions.
The 1150–1200 °C mode-I testing regime is outside the reported room-temperature-to-500 °C evidence range and is presented without supporting service or materials data.

High configurational entropy is asserted to create low-energy, chemically homogeneous grain boundaries, but neither this causal link nor grain-boundary energy was established by the cited study or any supplied prior evidence.

Matching grain size and thermomechanical processing would replace the actual comparison between an as-cast HEA and commercially sourced powder-sintered tungsten, so it does not reconstruct the reported intervention or baseline.

The hypothesis does not adequately explain the reported temperature-dependent plastic strain, strength retention, crack disappearance above 200 °C, or the role of the dendritic two-phase microstructure.
explanation: The response addresses the broad comparison of WTaTiVZr with tungsten and predicts improved crack resistance, but it substitutes a speculative grain-boundary-entropy mechanism for the reported interpretations involving multicomponent solid-solution strengthening, lattice distortion, Ti/V/Zr-associated ductility, localized deformation, and crack impediment. Its assumed homogeneous microstructure directly conflicts with the observed segregation. The proposed experiment is reasonably discriminating as a new study because it uses matched specimens, mode-I toughness, crack tracking, and microscopy with an explicit falsification rule. However, it cannot validate low grain-boundary energy merely from EBSD/TEM/EDS, and no supporting evidence is supplied. Most importantly, its temperature range, processing, baseline, and loading modes do not agree with the actual quasi-static compression, indentation through 500 °C, and room-temperature scratch measurements. It is therefore a novel but unsupported alternative rather than a reconstruction.
